title: Identifying the spatial pattern and driving factors of nitrate in groundwater using a novel framework of interpretable stacking ensemble learning
summary: An interpretable stacking ensemble mapped nitrate concentrations from 549 groundwater samples in Eden Valley. Spatial predictions estimated that 2.46% of sandstone aquifer area exceeded the cited drinking-water threshold and that 8.74% of high-prediction areas lay outside designated vulnerable zones. These are region-specific model estimates, not causal findings or new measurements.
ai_technology: The learned ensemble and SHAP ranked transmissivity, baseflow index, hydraulic conductivity, arable land and soil C:N as associated predictors.

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Models were evaluated by cross-validation and on held-out 2020–2021 wells; spatial estimates were derived from the fitted ensemble.
evidence.unknown: Predictions are geographically specific and depend on available well data; they do not establish contamination sources or measurements at unsampled locations.
